title: Ripples reflect a spectrum of synchronous spiking activity in human anterior temporal lobe (Tong et al., 2021): figure-level iEEG, micro-LFP and spiking arrays (derivative)
description: This derivative dataset repackages figure-level arrays from Tong et al. (2021), which examined hippocampal-adjacent anterior temporal lobe ripples in patients with drug-resistant epilepsy performing a paired-associates verbal memory task. It contains iEEG time-frequency power, ripple-band signals, ripple rasters, micro-LFP and sorted single-unit spiking data from 96-channel Utah microelectrode arrays, covering 7 participants. The arrays reproduce panels of Figures 1-4 of the article and support analyses linking ripples to synchronous spiking activity. Raw continuous recordings are not included.
methods_description: Participants with drug-resistant epilepsy were implanted with subdural and depth contacts, and six also had 96-channel microelectrode arrays in the anterior temporal lobe, at the NIH Clinical Center. iEEG was sampled at 1000 Hz and cleaned of line noise. Ripples were detected with an 80-120 Hz Butterworth band-pass and a Hilbert envelope threshold. Single units were obtained by threshold crossing and manual spike sorting, and analyses included Morlet wavelet power, spike rate and pairwise phase consistency.
